messages:
dmitri: quick canary run: separated prefill vs decode batching, added KV-aware enqueue gating (small window to favor warm KV hits). posting perf dump + flamegraph: https://perf.internal/runs/2318765432 :eyes:
infra-bot: job dmitri/canary-2318765432 started (canary target: 2% us-west-2)
dmitri: config nutshell: token_budget=32 for prefill, decode target=8, batch_cap=64, prefill gets higher priority when kv_warm_ratio < 0.6
sophia: nice — what exactly is the batch formation rule? milliseconds window?
dmitri: formation window = 15ms; handshake timeout 20ms for now. kv_gate drain_window_ms=50. snippet:
```
prefill:
  token_budget: 32
  priority: dynamic
decode:
  token_budget: 8
  batch_cap: 64
kv_gate:
  warm_threshold: 0.6
  drain_window_ms: 50
```
kyle: did you flip kernel affinity? that can change perf a lot for short sequences. cc @sophia
dmitri: yep — prefer fused-attn kernels for seq_len <= 256, fallback to generic path above that. microbench: decode p50 -12%, cpu/gpu utilization smoother.
chris: we saw past regressions where prefill-heavy bursts caused KV thrash and tail spikes. any sign of that?
dmitri: saw intermittent prefill steals that cause kv-cache churn. flamegraph shows spikes in KV lookup latency correlating with queue reshuffle. link above. plan: soft backoff on prefill when kv_miss_rate > 0.4 and route to slower kernel so head-of-line doesn't block decode.
sophia: p95 behavior? earlier results show p50 improves but p95 sometimes worsens. what do canary numbers say?
dmitri: current canary (2%): token cost -3.2%, p50 -9%, p95 +4%. investigating causes of p95 bump — hypothesis: batch handshake jitter + occasional kernel fallback cost.
kyle: try reducing handshake timeout to 5ms and increasing formation window to 15ms (or vice versa) to give more stable batches. also try micro-batching decode into smaller groups when KV warm ratio low.
dmitri: will run two variants: (A) handshake 5ms, window 15ms + kv soft-backoff; (B) handshake 10ms, window 25ms + kernel affinity relaxed.
chris: add rollout guard: auto-rollback if p95 > baseline * 1.1 for 10m, and alert if kv_warm_ratio < 0.5 for 5m.
sophia: agree. also add trace id tagging for any request hitting fallback kernel so we can correlate with client traces.
dmitri: adding metrics: route_kv_warm_ratio, route_kv_miss_rate, kernel_fallback_rate. will push dashboards.
sophia: thanks — keep us posted. :thumbsup:
infra-bot: deploy canary dmitri/canary-2318765432 succeeded in us-west-2 (2% traffic).
